recipes.name: Chicken Breast Cutlets with Artichokes and Capers
ingredients_raw: 1 cup whole wheat or white flour
0.125 teaspoon white pepper, or to taste
0.125 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
2 pounds chicken breast tenderloins or strips
1 (12 ounce) jar quartered marinated artichoke hearts, with liquid

steps.text: Combine flour, salt, and white and black peppers. Dredge chicken in seasoned flour and shake off excess.
Heat canola oil and olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts and cook until golden brown on both sides, and no longer pink on the inside; set aside.

Pour in chicken broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer, scraping the bottom of the pan to dissolve the caramelized bits. Add artichoke hearts and capers, return to a simmer, and cook until reduced by half.
Whisk butter into sauce until melted. Place cooked chicken back into pan, and simmer in the sauce for a few minutes to reheat. Serve on a platter sprinkled with chopped fresh parsley.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Breast Cutlets with Artichokes and Capers
raw_recipe.description: Golden brown chicken cutlets are served with a lemony artichoke and caper sauce in this straightforward and delicious chicken dish.

review.reviewBody: Hi everyone ... this is my recipe. The sauce is not supposed to be thick, but if you like it that way you can add a little cornstarch mixed with cold water, or make a roux (flour and butter). Also I use thin chicken breast cutlets not tenderloins (the allrecipes staff changed my recipe to tenderloins). Thanks for all the nice compliments - I am glad most of you liked this!

Love the flavors. I use regular chicken breasts instead of the tenders since they're always cheaper. Pound the chicken between sheets of plastic wrap to at least 1/2", cut into a few pieces, and cook in a couple batches. I find the pounding tenderizes the meat, and greatly improves the dish. Transfer to a pan in the oven to keep warm. Also, skip the salt in the flour mix. Plenty of salt in the capers and artichokes. If you want a thickened sauce, pour a little bit of the chicken broth into a small tupperware before adding it to the pan, add some of the leftover flour from the dredging (hey why waste it all?), close tightly, shake well and add to boiling sauce while stirring.

This isa new family favorite! I only had a pound and a half sized package of chicken on hand so I decided to add some fresh mushrooms ( 8 oz) and Julienned sun dried tomatoes (1oz) plus 1 Tbl butter to the pan right after taking the chicken out. When the mushrooms started browning I continued with the recipe. The dish was restaurant quality!

Excellent! Added some garlic powder and paprika to the flour. Pounded the cutlets for tenderness. Drained the artichokes. Used some corn starch to thicken the sauce. Put in fresh parsley. So delicious and so easy.

Made with 4 rounds of pounded chicken breasts. (Three full breasts in Bell and Evans organic. Cut breasts through lengthwise. Pounded. 3 minutes per side. Second addition of canola oil needed after two batches.) 1 cup chicken broth instead of two and added 1/3 cup white wine. Lemon slices added at time of artichokes. Served over thin spaghetti. Everything else same.

This was a superb recipe— easy, elegant, and delicious. I followed the recipe exactly, but I did add a healthy bunch of steamed baby spinach to the sauce after I added back the chicken (just because I needed to use it up). Some reviewers drained and rinsed the artichokes; I did NOT, and the sauce was delightfully tangy, but not overpowering. I served it over angel hair pasta, and had freshly grated cheese for those who wanted it. (The cheese was a fine addition, BTW.). One thing I would change: I only needed about half the flour and had to throw the rest away (I hated to waste it!), so I will prepare only a 1/2 cup of flour next time, but leave the salt and pepper amounts the same. This was a great recipe—thank you!

Wonderful recipe and fairly easy to make too! I always season my chicken before flouring, but the only other thing I did differently was to sub half the broth with Chardonnay. The taste is divine. If you want a thicker sauce, it's certainly easy to mix a tablespoon of corn starch with a half a cup of broth and mix it in with the sauce while it's at a boil. Thanks for a fantastic recipe!

Followed recipe but sauted onion and garlic first and fried the chicken with those. Also, I added diced marinated Greek olives and peperoncini to the mix and served over linguine noodles. Unbelievably delicious!!!

Excellent! I made it with the broth for the kids and they loved it. Chicken turned out tender. I skipped the canola oil and browned the chicken in olive oil plus 2 T butter, then added another tablespoon of butter at the end. I am planning to make this for a dinner party with white wine for part of the broth.

I have made this several times. both by following the recipe as written and making changes. Equally as good either way. Tonight I added a shallot some garlic, a splash of Marsala wine, and mushrooms. thickened the sauce a bit and served it over rice

I made this last night per the recipe. While the sauce was very flavorful it was pretty thin. I did reduce by half as instructed but that wasn't enough. It might be better to use less chicken broth or try to thicken it with a cornstarch slurry. Also, the chicken by itself was a little bland. The recipe calls for 1 cup of flour for dredging plus salt and pepper. I probably over 1/2 cup left after dredging the 2 lbs of tenders the recipe calls for. I think using 1/2 cup (or maybe 3/4 cup to be safe) plus the same amount of seasoning would make for better seasoned chicken.
I tried this recipe for the first time today and it was good. My husband had two plates. I'm keeping this one.

After reading other reviews I passed on using the artichoke "juice". In place of that I added white wine. We cooked some mushrooms and then serverd those on the side, but they were quickly added in after on the plate.

I liked it. Really good flavor. My wife not so much. The vinegar from the undrained artichoke hearts turned her off quite a bit. Just not her cup o tea. Very good will try with drained artichoke hearts next time.
What a great recipe. Easy as well! We added spinach and left out the parsley garnish.
I made this for my culinary club. 28 people loved it. It was fairly easy to do also.
My jar of artichokes was larger than the one on the ingredient list. Because of that , it had a bit more of the pickley juice than needed, but still delicious. Definitely going on the list.
My friends were super impressed! It was a hit. Will definitely make again.
